article_content: Dh'ainmich na poilis an dithis fhireannach a bhàsaich ann an Gleann Comhainn. Joe Mac a' Ghobhainn, 23 bliadhna, bha à Lancashire, ach' a' fuireach ann an ceann a tuath den Gleann. Bha e na bhall de Bhuidhinn Teasairginn Beinne Ghleann Comhainn. Sim MacDhaibhidh, 34 bliadhna, bha à Dun Edin. Chaidh an dithis a lorg le dithis shreapadairean eile aig Stob Coire nam Beithe feasgar Disathairne. Thug sgioba san robh buill de Bhuidhinn Teasairginn Beinne Ghleann Chomhainn agus na poilis na cuirp far na beinne. Thuirt ceannard buidheann theasairginn nam beann, Andy Nelson, nach robh comharran ann gun robh maoim-sneachda air a bhith ann. Tha Mgr Nelson ag ràdh gun robh ròp a' ceangal an dithis agus gur dòcha gun robh iad a' sreap nuair a thachair an tubaist. Bha iad uidheamachd fhreagarrach agus bha iad eòlach air a bhith a' sreap. Thèid aithisg gu Neach-casaid a' Chrùin.
translated_content: A police search located the body of a 23-year-old climber who lost his life in Glen Coe. Joe Mac a' Ghobhainn, originally from Lancashire but residing in the northern part of the glen, was a member of the Glencoe Mountain Rescue Team. Sim MacDhaibhidh, aged 34 and from the Edinburgh area, was also involved. The incident occurred during a descent from Stob Coire nam Beithe on Saturday afternoon. A joint effort by the Glencoe Mountain Rescue Team and Police Scotland recovered the body on the mountainside. Team leader Andy Nelson stated there were no indications of an avalanche, but it is suspected they may have slipped during the descent. They were seasoned climbers who understood the risks. The case will now be referred to the Procurator Fiscal.
